00346e5b90e2afa1: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2026 Amanah National Convention today passed a motion calling for the enactment of a Gender Parity Act in political representation to ensure that women make up at least 30 per cent of political candidates in the country.
The motion passed with 225 delegates voting aye and 164 nays.
Wanita Amanah chief Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu described the passage of the motion as a significant step forward in efforts to strengthen women's representation in the country's democracy.

She said women's participation in politics could no longer depend solely on discretion, limited opportunities or voluntary commitments, but must instead be strengthened through a clear and effective legal framework supported by an orderly implementation mechanism.
"The minimum 30 per cent target for female candidates is not a privilege, but an affirmative measure to ensure women have a fair opportunity to contribute, lead and shape the country's future.
"I would like to thank all delegates who tabled and supported this motion.
"May its approval serve as a starting point for more concrete action, rather than remaining merely a resolution on paper," she said in a Facebook post.

Aiman Athirah said the motion's approval also represented a political mandate from Amanah for the government to move from commitment to action, aspirations to legislation, and participation to meaningful representation.
"Amanah believes that democracy will never be truly complete as long as half of the country's leadership potential is not given the opportunity it deserves," she said.
77bdab2adc69c31b: KUALA LUMPUR: Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun signed off the season in style by winning their second World Tour men's doubles title at the Hong Kong Open on Sunday.
The Malaysian world No. 9 pair secured a 21-19, 21-18 win over Asian Games champions Leo Rolly Carnando-Daniel Marthin of Indonesia in the Super 500 final at Kai Tak Arena.
It was the French Open champions' second victory in three meetings against world No. 18 Leo Rolly-Daniel.
Wei Chong-Kai Wun's eighth World Tour title earned them US$39,500 (RM162,500), while Leo Rolly-Daniel had to settle for US$19,000 (RM78,200).

Meanwhile, Malaysia are on course for a double triumph as world No. 4 Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah take on Japan's world No. 11 pair Sumire Nakade-Miyu Takahashi in the women's doubles final later on Sunday.
5f52d11e81e34fd8: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Sepak Takraw Federation (MSTF) expects to revamp its coaching line-up for next season in a bid to further strengthen the national squad.
MSTF president Datuk Sumali Reduan said the national body is looking to add coaches across the board, not just the men's regu squad.
"We are looking to strengthen both the men's and women's elite squads as well as the backup squads," said Sumali yesterday.
"We are serious about improving our women's team and we have plans to hire a coach from Thailand to guide them.
"As for the men's squad, we have to keep working hard to maintain our performances.
"We also have to improve in newer events such as the quadrant, as well as chinlone which are a staple of multi-sport games today.
"We also have to strengthen our coaching for the backup squad to ensure that we continue to have talent for the future.
"We cannot afford to just focus on the men's regu squad, we have to look at all aspects."
Ahmad Jais Baharun, who is now technical director, will be overseeing development across the board.

After decades of playing bridesmaids to Thailand, the national men's squad won gold at last year's Thailand SEA Games, this year's Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, as well as the last two editions of the World Cup.
b5cee1caf9266c27: SHAH ALAM: The "big tent" proposal and other political strategies involving Pakatan Harapan should first be brought to its presidential council for discussion and not aired publicly, said DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke.

"Everyone has their own views and suggestions, but I believe that if we make suggestions publicly and discuss them through the media, we will not achieve the desired intentions or objectives," he told reporters after opening the Selangor DAP 2026 Convention here today.

He was commenting on Amanah secretary-general Muhammad Faiz Fadzil's suggestion that PH adopt a "big tent" approach and embrace more Malay-based parties to boost support among Malay voters ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16).
Loke also said DAP was open to the proposal for component parties to use their respective party logos in GE16, but this would require further discussions within PH before a final decision was made.
"What is most important is that we must consolidate our strength and find the best approach to face the election. However, such a proposal must first be discussed at the presidential council.
"DAP will give its views, and of course, we have suggestions on how to move forward in the coming election," he said.
On another matter, Loke said the status of his resignation as transport minister on Nov 10 was subject to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's decision.
"As far as I'm concerned, I already resigned," he said.
Anwar had previous said the government need not rush into deciding on Loke's resignation, although the official letter on the matter had been received, adding that it required careful consideration.

The previous day, Loke had reiterated his decision to stand by his resignation with immediate effect following the High Court's decision to allow former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.

eee81a086a0d4476: KULIM: Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's daughter, who was injured in a motorcycle crash on Nov 12, was discharged from hospital yesterday.

a46f093d4acc743c: SEREMBAN: Drug trafficking syndicates are increasingly using social media and closed-group applications to market electronic cigarettes (vapes) containing synthetic drugs, locally known as 'piu-piu', with the products delivered to buyers, including students, through courier and delivery services.

Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the modus operandi allowed transactions to take place without direct contact between sellers and buyers, making it more difficult for the police to detect such activities.

"Communication between sellers and buyers takes place through specific platforms, including dark web sites, which act as intermediaries and allow them to connect discreetly to obtain the illicit substances.

"Payments are made online, after which the products are delivered to buyers through e-hailing or courier services. Based on our intelligence, a single cartridge is sold for between RM50 and RM100, depending on its quality and contents," he told Bernama.
He said the misuse of vapes containing drug-laced liquids, or 'piu-piu', was first detected in Negri Sembilan last year and has since emerged as a growing concern, particularly among students.
Alzafny said police had identified three cases involving secondary school students in the state over the past three years, comprising one case in May and two others early this month.
Tests on the seized vape liquids found that they contained various drugs, including methamphetamine, methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) and ketamine, he added.
It was reported that a 17-year-old male student in Nilai had tested positive for three types of drugs, namely ketamine, benzodiazepines and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC).
The student is being investigated following the circulation of a video on social media showing him in an intoxicated state, allegedly after using a vape.

Meanwhile, Alzafny said family-related problems and emotional stress were among the factors that could lead individuals to misuse drug-laced vapes, with some turning to the substances in an attempt to relieve stress.
"They may also use these vapes in search of new experiences because they produce an intoxicating effect, unlike ordinary vapes," he said.
He said teenagers were also attracted to the devices' modern designs, appealing scents and portability, which made them easy to conceal.
Alzafny said all district police chiefs had been instructed to intensify surprise inspections at schools, particularly in hostel areas.
Police would also introduce a 'Heart to Heart' programme featuring open discussions between officers and students to raise awareness of the dangers of drug abuse.

He urged local authorities to review permits issued for vape sales, particularly to ensure that students could not easily access the products, and advised parents to take a more active role in monitoring their children's social circles.
"Parents should also regularly check their children's personal belongings, such as school bags, to determine whether they possess vape devices or are involved in drug abuse.
"Early warning signs include behavioural changes, such as a loss of self-control or actions that are out of character," he said.

Commenting on the supply of drug-laced vape products in the state, Alzafny said police had recently arrested two foreign nationals and seized 732 cartridges containing a total of 7,320 millilitres of a substance suspected to be ketamine, worth RM219,600, at a residence in the Klang Valley last October.

He said those involved in supplying or distributing vape liquids containing drugs could face action under the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, while students found to be involved would be referred to the National Anti-Drug Agency (Nada) for treatment and rehabilitation.

c407a00034cd12b8: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Football League (MFL) has confirmed that DPMM's Argentine-born striker Rodrigo Holgado will be eligible to play immediately once the formalities are completed.

MFL chief executive officer Shazli Shaik clarified that the 31-year-old forward does not have to wait for the mid-season transfer window to make his debut for the Brunei-based outfit because he is an unattached free agent.
"Not yet, in the registration process. If complete registration, can play at any time," Shazli told Timesport.
A check by Timesport on the FA of Malaysia's (FAM) Competitions Management System (CMS) on Sunday showed that Holgado had yet to be registered in DPMM's squad list.

Under normal circumstances, M-League teams looking to reinforce their squads must wait for the designated registration periods. For the 2026-2027 season, the second transfer window will open from Jan 5 to Feb 1, 2027.
However, league regulations allow clubs to register unattached free agents outside the designated transfer windows, subject to the necessary clearance from the league and governing bodies.

DPMM recently revealed that it had received the green light to bring in Holgado after the forward completed a 12-month FIFA suspension over the falsification of eligibility documents involving the national team. The suspension, which was upheld by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ended on Oct 31.

The former America de Cali and Coquimbo Unido striker is expected to bolster DPMM's attack alongside imports Dalberto Luan and Jordan Murray, although his match fitness remains a question after a year away from competitive football.

2540bea22252b742: SHAH ALAM: DAP is in “crisis mode” and needs to change its approach and develop new strategies ahead of future elections, says its secretary-general, Loke Siew Fook.
Loke said the party appeared to have grown complacent and lost the fighting spirit it had when it helped Pakatan Harapan capture Selangor in 2008.

“We are in crisis mode. Others want to bring down our party and our government. We must take our struggle seriously and rediscover the spirit of defending and fighting for our cause that we had in 2008.
“Before winning in 2008, everyone was spirited. After winning, we seemed to have grown comfortable. We must guard against this and remain vigilant,” he said at the Selangor DAP convention here today.

Loke acknowledged that PH faced challenges in Selangor, including changes in the state's voter demographics as people from the four opposition-led states - Kedah, Kelantan, Terengganu and Perlis - moved there for work and subsequently transferred their voter registration to Selangor.
“This is a strategy being planned and implemented. It is a major challenge for Selangor PH, and we must find ways to address it.
“What is important is how we inspire Selangor voters to see PH as the choice to continue leading the state,” he said.
Loke said political developments in several states, including Melaka and Negeri Sembilan, showed that good governance alone was insufficient to secure electoral victories.
This was evident from the way Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional had managed to consolidate their support and capitalise on anti-DAP sentiment, he said.
Loke warned that losing Selangor in the next election would not only cost PH control of the state government, but would also jeopardise the progress the coalition has made since 2008.
“If we lose our strength or mandate in Selangor, everything achieved over the past 18 years since 2008 could be lost,” he said.
“The gains we have made would be undone. We want to keep moving forward, not backwards.”

DAP has faced significant electoral setbacks following its strong showing in the August 2023 six-state elections, when it won 46 of the 47 seats it contested across Penang, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Kedah.
It suffered a complete defeat in last November’s Sabah election, losing all eight seats it contested, including four it previously held, to BN.
DAP won just six of the 17 seats it contested in July's Johor election, including losing four it previously held, to Barisan Nasional.
The party won nine of the 11 seats it contested in the Negeri Sembilan election in August, but PH lost control of the state after securing only 11 of the 36 seats.
DAP retained all four seats it previously held in Saturday's Melaka polls, but failed to win any of the three additional seats it contested.

17861e37d8695a91: KOTA BARU: Flooding could hit Jeli, Pasir Mas, Tanah Merah and Tumpat in Kelantan from Nov 24 to 27, according to the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID).

In its preliminary flood forecast for Kelantan today, the department said its analysis of hydrological data using a flood forecasting model identified flood hotspots, low-lying areas and other flood-prone locations in the four districts as particularly at risk.

The department said flooding could occur earlier or later than forecast and advised disaster management agencies and residents, particularly those in areas likely to be affected, to stay alert and follow instructions from the authorities.
DID said it would continue monitoring the river basins concerned and issue flood warnings if heavy rain persisted.
In Jeli, the areas at risk are in the Sungai Golok basin and include Sungai Buloh, Sungai Lanas, Sungai Legeh and Sungai Satan.

In Pasir Mas, the areas at risk include Sungai Golok, Sungai Bunut Susu, Sungai Meranti, Sungai Tandak, Sungai Kedotok, Sungai Lanchang, Tasik Garu, Tasik Danau To' Uban, Sungai Rengas, Sungai Lemal and Sungai Lemal Mati.
The forecast for Tanah Merah covers Sungai Golok, Sungai Jegor, Sungai Manal, Sungai Jedok, Sungai Air Bujing and Sungai Lanas.
In Tumpat, the department identified Sungai Golok, Sungai Pengkalan Nangka, Sungai Mentua, Sungai Gali, Sungai Kelaboran and Sungai Tapang as areas at risk.
The public can check the latest flood information and warnings at publicinfobanjir.water.gov.my or on the PublicInfoBanjir Facebook page.
6a22327f42c13926: KUALA LUMPUR: Former national singles star Ong Ewe Hock has finally won an Asian title, 27 years after settling for silver at the Asian Championships.

The 54-year-old partnered Goh Cheng Huan to beat Thailand's Visava Pimsamarn-Nuttawut Sroidokson 21-8, 21-14 in the men's doubles 50-plus final at the Badminton Asia Senior Championships in Gwangju, South Korea, on Sunday.
It was a different competition and discipline from the one in which Ewe Hock fell short in 1999, when he lost the Asian Championships men's singles final to China's Chen Hong in Kuala Lumpur.
"I never won the Asian Championships before and only managed to get silver," said Ewe Hock.
"Now the target is to get first place."
Ewe Hock and Cheng Huan had previously won bronze in the 50-plus men's doubles at the 2025 World Senior Championships in Pattaya, Thailand.
The former national shuttler said last year that he wanted to win the 2027 edition of the world senior meet.
He said the experience in Pattaya had encouraged him to continue competing when he had the time.
"After finishing third at the World Senior Championships last year, I had a feeling that if there was another opportunity, I would go and play," he said.
"If I have time, I can take part in a few more competitions like this."
Despite the final score, Ewe Hock said he and Cheng Huan had to work hard against their Thai opponents.
"There were a lot of rallies, even though the score didn't look close," he said.
"In the second game, we were level at 13-13 and 14-14."
Ewe Hock, who is also a coach, said he would take a short break before deciding on his next competition.

96ee7c10883fc813: KUALA LUMPUR: Smartphone users whose devices do not meet the minimum specifications for the disaster early warning system will not be left out of emergency alerts, as notifications via short message service (SMS) will continue to be available.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the existing notification mechanism operated by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) would continue as usual to ensure all segments of society received timely warnings.

"So, the SMS notification system is still in place, and Nadma can certainly implement it. It is already available now," he told a press conference after attending the closing ceremony of the MYReaders Lembah Pantai 2026 programme.

He said the Early Warning System (EWS) developed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) would not replace existing mechanisms but would complement them to strengthen the dissemination of disaster information to the public.
Fahmi said in areas prone to flooding, particularly along river corridors, the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) had installed warning sirens as part of its preparedness measures.

On Nov 19, MCMC urged smartphone users to update their devices to support EWS alerts, with the minimum requirements being an iPhone 11 or newer running iOS 27.2 or later, Android phones running Android 12 or later, and Huawei devices running EMUI 16 or later.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said an initial EWS test would be conducted specifically at Parliament tomorrow about 1.30pm.
The exercise would allow MPs to see how alert notifications appeared on their mobile phones before informing their constituents and explaining how the system worked.
He said a full-scale test of the system was scheduled to be conducted simultaneously nationwide on Nov 29, with the time to be confirmed soon.
9255056f29307d5f: TURKIYE: The COP31 presidency proposed an eleventh-hour deal Sunday that again fails to mention fossil fuels -- an omission that deepened a tense standoff at the UN climate talks.

The latest offering by summit co-hosts Turkey and Australia published deep into overtime leaves unresolved tensions over planet-heating fossil fuels but retains a much-sought goal to electrify the global economy.
The proposal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations at a closing session Sunday but they have struggled to bridge differences during two weeks of grinding negotiations.
The European Union and other nations have pushed for strong language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, a call that has faced resistance from oil-rich Saudi Arabia.
An EU official told AFP the latest proposal was a "backwards" step, warning there was a "very real possibility" that COP31 ends with no deal.
"I am more pessimistic today than I was yesterday," the official said on condition of anonymity.
"The situation is difficult, and the outcome is uncertain. The oil-producing countries are putting up a fierce fight," a German official said.
A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP.
Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks and the summit comes against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.
A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase out of fossil fuels but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas.
Threats of a walkout prompted Turkey and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the European Union and Saudi Arabia in a bid to broker a compromise.
The latest text introduces a reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels -- but stops short of naming them explicitly.
And it retains a contentious push to expand carbon capture and storage, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions.
"We are very disappointed with how the text looks," the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Michael Joseph, told AFP after leaving the COP31 presidency's offices.
"I can't honestly say that I'm okay with it passing" in its current state, Joseph said, adding that the draft was "quite silent" on fossil fuels.
GOAL TO ELECTRIFY
The draft also calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 and the expansion of "clean energy".
The summit had been under pressure to show progress in tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia.
Facing blowback over fossil fuels, Turkey and Australia pointed to "electrification" as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security.
This works by replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels directly -- like diesel cars and gas heating -- with electric alternatives.
But some nations had demanded an explicitly "clean" target to ensure the electrification push was powered by renewable energy and not fossil fuels.
Around one-third of global electricity is produced using coal and another fifth using fossil gas.

Attempts by Saudi Arabia, India and Kenya meanwhile to delay the next set of reports by the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) have been another major source of friction at the talks.
The draft text "highlights the importance" of these reports for an upcoming stocktake of global carbon-cutting efforts in 2028.
Dozens of countries across Europe, Africa and the Pacific want these assessments by the global scientific authority on climate change published in time for that crucial stocktake.
Countries have also disagreed at COP31 over how to respond to the looming breach of the 1.5C warming target set under the Paris climate accord.
The latest draft expressed "deep concern" that global warming would cross 1.5C above pre-industrial levels in the next few years.
The talks also jammed over long-running complaints that rich nations are shirking their obligations to help developing nations confront climate change.
The removal of a $120 billion target for climate adaptation angered developing nations.

09938a90d76ab7f7: KUALA LUMPUR: Honda Malaysia Racing Team (HMRT) ended an 11-year wait to recapture the Sepang 1,000 Kilometres (S1K) title with a well-deserved win in the nation's premier endurance race late yesterday.

HMRT drivers Putera Adam Halim, Avila Bahar and their No. 27 Honda Civic (M-Production class) were close to flawless as they took the flag in eight hours, 16 minutes and 19.311 seconds (181 laps) to claim the overall win under the Sepang Circuit floodlights.

Two-time defending champions Hi-Rev Dream Chaser (Daim Hishamuddin, Aaron Hakim, Lee Wai Cong) were forced to settle for second (175 laps) this time while Tedco Racing's Foo Yung Chieh, Freddie Ang, Yee Kok Jun and Goh Lee Heng rounded out the podium after completing 174 laps.
Axle Sports (Alister Yoong, Naquib Azlan, Nabil Azlan) were just off the podium in fourth (173 laps) with Dream Chaser's second car (Rahul Mayer, Mark Darwin, Lew Karwai), 33.637s adrift of them.
The win capped a strong season for HMRT, with Indonesian driver Avila also winning the Malaysian Touring Car Championship title with them earlier this year.
"The hard work and dedication of everyone at HMRT made it possible for us to win both the MTCC title and the S1K title in the same year," said Avila.
"It was a privilege to share the car with Aaron Lim in MTCC and Putera Adam in S1K. I am very proud of what we have achieved together."
Meanwhile, Axle Sports team principal Alex Yoong was pleased with his team's performances in their Proton S70.
"Finishing fourth at the S1K is a fantastic result for a car we've only recently developed," said Alex.

"We came into this programme knowing there would be a steep learning curve, so to go from a podium at MTCC in August to fourth place at the S1K is a real testament to the hard work of our engineers, mechanics and the entire team."
Axle Sports had spent months developing the S70 platform for endurance racing locally.
0a59634d1718224f: SHAH ALAM: Setiausaha Agung DAP, Loke Siew Fook menegur tahap kehadiran perwakilan pada Konvensyen DAP Selangor yang disifatkannya kurang memberangsangkan, selepas banyak kerusi kosong ketika beliau sedang berucap.
Loke yang dilihat tidak berpuas hati dengan keadaan itu juga meminta pengerusi DAP Selangor menyemak senarai ketua kampung dan ahli majlis serta nama Adun yang tidak hadir diserahkan kepadanya.
Katanya, cawangan parti ditubuhkan bukan semata-mata untuk menghadapi pemilihan, sebaliknya berperanan membawa obor perjuangan parti.

"Kehadiran tidak begitu memberangsangkan kerana tak ada pemilihan parti. Kalau pemilihan parti tak payah cakap pun dewan penuh," katanya ketika berucap merasmikan konvensyen itu di Selangor International Trade Center.

Beliau berkata, ketidakhadiran pemegang jawatan yang dilantik atau dipilih mencerminkan kegagalan memenuhi tanggungjawab asas, justeru tindakan sewajarnya perlu dipertimbangkan terhadap mereka yang tidak menunjukkan komitmen.
"Kalau ahli majlis tak hadir, senarai hitam dia. Jangan sambung. Kalau tak ada komitmen kepada parti tak payah bagi peluang kedua.

"Kalau mana-mana Adun tak hadir hari ini bagi nama kepada saya. Ini tanggungjawab asas. Kalau komitmen yang paling asas tak ada jangan cakap pasal perjuangan. Jangan cakap pasal nak jadi calon," katanya.
Loke berkata beliau bersedia mengambil pendirian tegas berhubung disiplin parti walaupun tindakannya mungkin tidak disenangi sesetengah pihak.

Beliau turut memberi amaran bahawa mereka yang tidak menunjukkan komitmen terhadap parti tidak akan diberikan kerusi untuk bertanding pada pilihan raya akan datang, tanpa mengira pengaruh mereka dalam cawangan atau kalangan perwakilan.

ca4b68116abf69d9: KUALA LUMPUR: BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has called on Umno and MCA youth wings to work together ahead of the next general election (GE16).

He said both wings should avoid letting disagreements over a proposal to reinstate local government elections in the Federal Territories cause friction, as Umno and MCA were part of the same BN family.
"Umno Youth and MCA Youth, do not fight. Time is running out. We are brothers and sisters in the BN family.
"I respect both MCA Youth and Umno Youth," he said in his speech at the opening of the fourth general assembly of the 30th MCA Central Delegates at Wisma MCA here today.
Zahid said cooperation among BN component parties needed to be strengthened through mutual respect, including allowing each party to express its views.
"If there are views that are not clear, let us explain them. If there is no agreement, let us sit together and find a solution now.
"Do not wait any longer. Believe me, we do not have much time," he said.
Earlier, MCA Youth chief Ling Tian Soon called on the government to revive local government elections, starting in the Federal Territories, when addressing the MCA Youth general assembly.
He said the elections would give residents the opportunity to choose their own representatives, just as voters in other states elect members of their respective state legislative assemblies.
Umno has repeatedly opposed proposals to revive local government elections, citing concerns that they would increase taxpayers' financial burden and could deepen racial polarisation.
Zahid said differences of opinion among BN component parties should not lead to divisions but should instead be used to strengthen the coalition.
"Although we come from different backgrounds, we have responsibilities towards the communities we represent.
"However, we are willing to sit together and work towards a common goal.
"If we could do it in the past, why can we not do it now?" he said.
b8b16d2c0c6bfa0f: LONDON: A diamond ring worn by one of the most famous survivors of the sinking of the Titanic has sold for £150,000 (US$165,000) at auction, PA Media/dpa reported.
Lucy, Lady Duff Gordon was wearing the solitaire diamond ring when the passenger liner sank during its maiden voyage on April 15 1912 – with the loss of around 1,500 lives.
It was the only piece of jewellery she owned of any significance to survive the sinking.
Within the Duff Gordon family it was known as The Titanic Ring and was believed to have been her engagement ring.
The ring was sold via direct descendant and was given to Lady Duff Gordon's grandson John, the 3rd Earl of Halsbury, a British crossbencher peer and scientist.
Upon his death it stayed within the family and has been treasured ever since.
The ring went under the hammer at Henry Aldridge & Son in Devizes, Wiltshire on Saturday.
In 1912 Lady Duff Gordon travelled to the United States (US) with husband, Sir Cosmo, as first class passengers on board the Titanic.
During the evacuation, the Duff Gordons and secretary Laura Mabel Francatelli escaped in Lifeboat No 1.
Although the boat was designed to hold 40 people, it was lowered with only 12 people aboard – seven of them crew.
While on RMS Carpathia, the Cunard liner that rescued Titanic survivors, Sir Cosmo presented each of the men from Lifeboat No 1 with a cheque for £5.
This was to help them after the White Star Line stopped their wages when the Titanic sank.
This led to gossip the Duff Gordons had bribed their lifeboat's crew not to return to save swimmers out of fear the vessel would be swamped.
Meanwhile, a unique day ticket to view the Titanic on the day of its departure from Southampton sold for £40,000.
The ticket allowed the mother of a second class passenger to watch the departure of the liner.
The card bears the White Star burgee and is addressed to the officer in charge.
It states: "Please allow Mr Talbot and 2 friends to view the S.S. Titanic."
It is stamped "second-class" and is dated April 10 1912.
A handwritten note on the reverse says: "Mrs Dibden plus two sisters."
It was carried onto the Titanic by Eliza Dibden, the mother of 18-year-old William Dibden, from the New Forest, Hampshire, who perished in the disaster.
Accompanying the ticket is her son's first communion certificate dated Easter 1908.
Meanwhile, a postcard written by the Titanic's senior wireless operator when the liner was docked at Southampton sold for £32,000.
Jack Phillips, 25, wrote the card – featuring a photograph of the Titanic on the front – to his sister Elsie Phillips on April 6 1912.

Phillips, described by auctioneer Andrew Aldridge as "one of the true heroes of the disaster," sent wireless messages enlisting other ships to assist with rescuing passengers and crew as the Titanic was sinking.
The postcard, addressed to Miss Elsie Phillips of Godalming, Surrey, features a photo of the Titanic at Southampton.
It reads: "Thanks very much for your letter. Having glorious weather, went to Cowes yesterday. Will write later before we sail."
The sale totals include buyer's premium.

ef667054a60ea7bf: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Darul Ta'zim's (JDT) premium streaming platform, JDT+, has released a teaser for "Outbound", its documentary series following the club's campaign in the Asian Champions League Elite (ACLE).

The teaser, shared on social media via @watchjdtplus, features audio from a news bulletin about FIFA's disciplinary action against the FA of Malaysia (FAM) and seven players over falsified eligibility documents.
The controversy arose after documents submitted during the eligibility process for the seven foreign-born players were found to have been falsified.
The players involved were Joao Figueiredo, Jon Irazabal, Hector Hevel, Gabriel Arrocha, Facundo Garces, Rodrigo Holgado and Imanol Machuca.

In March 2026, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) partially upheld the players' appeals, ruling that their 12-month suspensions would apply only to official matches, not all football-related activities. The Court dismissed FAM's appeal, leaving its CHF350,000 fine unchanged.
The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) subsequently ruled that Malaysia had forfeited its 2027 Asian Cup qualifying matches against Nepal and Vietnam, recording 3-0 defeats in both fixtures.
JDT had previously expressed disappointment over the documentation issue, which affected several of its players.
Club chief executive Luis Garcia spoke about the consequences of the case, while club owner and Regent of Johor, Tunku Ismail Sultan Ibrahim, had also commented publicly on the matter.
According to JDT+, Outbound is an annual documentary series following the club's journey in the ACLE.
The series is told across three episodes, with each season forming a separate chapter featuring the club's opponents, changing squads, setbacks and progress in continental competition.
The platform's official description states that the series captures JDT's campaign against leading teams across Asia as the club continues its pursuit of becoming a force in continental football.
Outbound is to stream exclusively on JDT+ in November.
3595e280c5f1929f: KUALA LUMPUR: Penduduk Palestin berdepan kekurangan bekalan air bersih dan selamat yang serius apabila rejim Zionis terus memperketat kawalan terhadap sumber air di seluruh wilayah Palestin diduduki, sekali gus menjadikannya strategi untuk memaksa penduduk meninggalkan kediaman mereka.

Ketua Pengarah Perancangan dan Dasar Palestin, Adel Yasin, berkata sejak pendudukan Israel pada Jun 1967, penduduk Palestin dihalang membangunkan sumber air sendiri, manakala semua sumber air berada di bawah kawalan langsung Israel.

"Penduduk Palestin hanya mendapat tiga hingga lima liter air minuman seorang sehari berbanding kira-kira 100 liter yang diperlukan bagi setiap individu untuk menjalani kehidupan sihat berdasarkan laporan Pertubuhan Bangsa-bangsa Bersatu (PBB)," katanya dalam wawancara bersama Bernama TV dari Palestin baru-baru ini.

Adel yang juga jurucakap rasmi Pihak Berkuasa Air Palestin berkata, berdasarkan laporan Bank Dunia dan PBB, kira-kira 90% infrastruktur bekalan air di Gaza mengalami kerosakan menyeluruh sejak Oktober 2023.
Jelasnya, Israel turut menghalang kemasukan bahan penting seperti konkrit, bahan api dan keluli yang diperlukan untuk membina semula kemudahan bekalan air di Gaza.
Menurutnya, keadaan di Tebing Barat semakin meruncing apabila rejim Israel turut menguasai sumber air bawah tanah.
"Penduduk Palestin terpaksa mendapatkan bekalan air daripada lori tangki yang datang dari lokasi jauh, namun kaedah itu juga tidak selamat kerana mudah menjadi sasaran serangan tentera udara Israel."
Beliau berkata, beberapa petugas Pihak Berkuasa Air Palestin turut terbunuh ketika menjalankan kerja penyelenggaraan atau membaiki kemudahan bekalan air.

Adel turut mendedahkan keadaan sebuah keluarga Palestin di Hebron hanya menerima bekalan air sekali setiap 60 hari pada musim panas dan 30 hari pada musim sejuk, sedangkan penempatan Israel di kawasan sama menikmati bekalan air sepanjang masa.
"Ini bermakna masalah berkenaan bukan berpunca daripada kekurangan sumber air secara semula jadi, sebaliknya krisis akibat tindakan manusia dan dikawal oleh Israel.
"Jelas sekali mereka menggunakan air sebagai senjata untuk memaksa penduduk Palestin berpindah."
d89e46d77dad69ee: PETALING JAYA: The minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) meeting concerning Najib Razak’s house arrest were declassified to enable the Attorney-General’s Chambers to prepare an affidavit in response to a judicial review filed by the Malaysian Bar, says Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
The home minister said the minutes needed to be included in the government’s affidavit to address the legal challenge, reported Bernama.
“The document must first be declassified to enable the attorney-general to prepare an affidavit in reply.
“The affidavit will only be complete if the matters discussed at the FTPB meeting are included in it,” he told reporters at a police fun run in Kuala Lumpur today.

On Nov 19, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the document containing the order for Najib to be placed under house arrest was classified under the Official Secrets Act, but that declassification was not unusual when such documents were challenged in court.
However, he did not confirm whether the document had been declassified, saying the government would provide an update on the matter soon.
On Nov 10, the Malaysian Bar filed for leave to challenge the FTPB’s proceedings on Sept 18, which decided to allow Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest.
A source previously told FMT that the minutes of the FTPB meeting were among the documents to be included in the AGC’s affidavit in connection the Malaysian Bar’s challenge.
The source also said Cabinet approval for the declassification was not required, citing Section 2C of the Official Secrets Act 1972.

The meeting’s minutes recorded objections from Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar and federal territories minister Hannah Yeoh to a proposal to allow Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.

The Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, took the decision to place Najib under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine imposed on the former Umno president and other conditions.
Najib was subsequently transferred to his home in Taman Duta, Kuala Lumpur, now gazetted as a prison, after the fine was settled through funds raised by Umno.

88c5aad8c93500aa: KUALA LUMPUR: MBSB Research has raised its forecast for Malaysia's export growth in 2026 to 39 per cent from 32 per cent previously.
This follows stronger-than-expected shipments in October, particularly of electrical and electronics (E&E) products.

The firm also revised its import growth forecast upwards to 31 per cent from 26 per cent, citing sustained demand for production materials and machinery amid strong manufacturing and investment activities.
The upward revisions came after Malaysia's exports surged 61.1 per cent year-on-year in October, the fastest growth since April 2021, compared with 54.9 per cent in September.
Imports also accelerated, rising 54.4 per cent against 52.7 per cent in the preceding month, bringing total trade growth to 58 per cent from 53.9 per cent previously.

"The latest data continued to indicate that Malaysia's external trade sustained robust performance mainly driven by E&E products, as well as higher shipments of processed petroleum and palm oil products and liquefied natural gas (LNG)," MBSB Research said.
The firm said shipments increased 87.2 per cent, accounting for about 64.5 per cent of the overall increase in exports during the month.

The strong performance was also reflected in shipments to major trading partners, particularly Taiwan, where exports jumped 292.6 per cent, while shipments to the United States increased 107.8 per cent.
Exports to India grew 117.3 per cent, while shipments to China rose 34.8 per cent.
The firm said exports to Asean strengthened 53.9 per cent, supported by higher shipments to Indonesia and Singapore.
On a monthly basis, exports grew 10.9 per cent in October, supported by an 11.1 per cent increase in manufactured goods, including a 13.9 per cent rise in E&E products.
The stronger export performance helped widen Malaysia's trade surplus to RM41.8 billion in October, its highest level in four months, compared with RM34.4 billion in September.
"For the first 10 months of 2026, total trade expanded 33.2 per cent to exceed RM3 trillion, reaching the milestone two months earlier than in 2025," MBSB Research added.
Exports grew 37.1 per cent during the period, while imports increased 28.8 per cent.
The cumulative trade surplus more than doubled to RM274.8 billion from RM128.3 billion a year earlier.
On the import front, MBSB Research said purchases of intermediate goods, which are materials used in production, remained strong, rising 64 per cent in October.
Imports of capital goods, including machinery and equipment used by businesses, increased 32.9 per cent, pointing to sustained investment-related demand.
However, the firm cautioned that the positive trade outlook remained exposed to uncertainties surrounding US trade policies, weaker global demand, supply chain disruptions and higher operating costs.
"We expect trade momentum to remain robust in the final two months of 2026.
"Nevertheless, uncertainties surrounding US trade policies, risk of softer global demand, supply chain disruptions and elevated costs remain key downside risks," the firm said.

It added that higher imports of intermediate materials and capital goods could also limit further expansion in the trade surplus, although demand for E&E products, palm oil and LNG should continue to support Malaysia's external trade.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

68f81dff376d18f7: KUALA LUMPUR: Head coach Shukor Adan hinted at uncertainties about his future with the national Under-17 setup, and said that Malaysia must improve its tournament preparation if its age-group teams are to bridge the gap at continental level.

Malaysia secured qualification after beating Laos 2-1 in their final Group H match in Vientiane in September, finishing among the seven best runners-up in the qualifiers.

132a64088322210a: A man who heroically tackled a gunman at a Jewish festival on Bondi Beach said his wounds still ache as he issued a plea for unity almost a year after Australia's worst mass shooting in decades.
Fruit seller Ahmed al Ahmed, who was born in Syria and moved to Australia in 2006, was visiting the Sydney beach with his cousin on a Sunday afternoon last December when he heard shots ring out.
He rushed to tackle one of the gunmen as they fired round after round into a crowd of men, women and children.
"I didn't think about it," he told AFP.
"Because to save people's lives, there's no need to think, when you hear the kids and the women and old people and men and everyone asking for help."
"Every human has a secret courage in his heart. It comes in the time when needed, when it's asked.
"I heard people asking, and I did it."
Fifteen people were killed and dozens were wounded on Dec 14, 2025, as crowds gathered at the world-famous beach to celebrate Hanukkah.
An elderly woman also died this month from complications linked to her wounds.
Ahmed's actions have been credited with stopping many more from dying after video of his act of bravery taken by a bystander went viral.
The father of two was lauded as a "true Australian hero" by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and a fundraising campaign raised millions of dollars.
But Ahmed said much of the initial fame passed him by – he was too focused on recovering from the devastating wounds he suffered.
Face to face with a killer
Tackling the gunman and wrestling the rifle from his hands, Ahmed said he found himself face to face with the killer – a memory that still haunts him "day by day, night by night."
"He was thinking he's a god, and no one can touch him," he said.
In that moment Ahmed was aiming the gun at the shooter.
"I asked him: 'leave, leave'," he said. "I don't wanna shoot."
The shooter retreated, leaving Ahmed to take cover behind a tree, where he came under fire.
"I start feeling my whole clothes get wet, you know, similar like someone taking a bucket of blood and threw it on you," he said.
"And then I start feeling: 'Oh, I'm gonna die. Oh my God, my kids, my family, my wife. What's happened?'"
The man he tackled, Sajid Akram, was killed by police at the scene.
His son, Naveed, remains in custody facing a total of 78 charges, including terrorism and murder. He has yet to enter a plea.
Two of the five bullets that struck Ahmed that day are still inside him.
He is on medication for nerve pain and to help him sleep, with the mobility of his left hand still limited.
"I'm still suffering," said Ahmed, who focused his energies on writing a book – "Light Will Win" – that was released this month.
He is also setting up a foundation to help women and children trapped in violence, inspired by his own difficult upbringing as the son of a police officer in Syria.
He told AFP he wouldn't do it any differently if he relived that fateful day, despite his wounds.
"I've been chosen. God chose me for that and to lead our community not to be divided," Ahmed said.
'We are human beings'
The Bondi shooting – one of the worst attacks on Jews worldwide since the Oct 7 killings by Hamas in Israel – changed Australia forever.
The ruling Labor Party announced a crackdown on gun ownership and new laws allowing them to ban extremist political groups.
However, Australia has also since seen a surge in support for Pauline Hanson's far-right One Nation party, which has vowed sweeping cuts to immigration, especially from "radical Islamic countries."
For Ahmed – a Muslim and an immigrant – such politics have no place in the country he calls home.
"I'm a proud Aussie," he said.
"One Nation – it's wrong, wrong, wrong, wrong."
"We have to respect each other. We have to care about each other."

"You know, we are human beings. No matter where you come from, no matter what your colour, what you are, what's your religion, we have to treat each other with respect, and don't judge and blame others."
"Australia is multicultural."
Equating the actions of the two shooters at Bondi with his religion – as many have – is unthinkable for Ahmed.
"This is not a Muslim," he said. "I'm a Muslim, and I put my life in danger."
"I never heard my religion say to kill innocent people. That's not right."

402e4abf38c942a1: In South Asia, survivors of sexual and physical abuse are often met with judgment and stigma
Originally published on Global Voices
Photo via Pratistha Gautam. Used with permission.
Editorial note: This article contains mention of gender-based violence, sexual assault, violence against children, and child sexual abuse, which may be triggering for some readers.

November 25 to December 10, 2026, marks the UN’s 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence. However, even as gender-based violence gets more recognition globally, survivors are still struggling to access social or legal justice. South Asia is no exception to this. Global Voices sat down with one survivor of childhood abuse who uses her experience to fuel her advocacy work today.

South Asia is home to nearly one quarter of the world’s population, woven with a diverse, culture-driven fabric where women are often celebrated as goddesses. However, this veneration doesn’t necessarily mean South Asian women are safe or free from abuse.

In Nepal, there are far too many examples of crimes against women and girls. For instance, Nirmala Panta, 13, was found dead in a sugarcane field — a case which has remained unsolved since 2018. Bhagirathi Bhatta, 17, was choked to death when returning home from school in 2021, and Inisha BK, 16, was found unconscious in the Janagaran Community Forest in Surkhet in early 2026. A similar yet shocking case is that of a 3-year-old Garima, who was found dead inside an abandoned house in Jeetpur in southern Nepal. While these tragic rape and murder cases leave deep scars in Nepal’s national psyche, even more cases go unheard and unreported.

Sparking a nationwide outrage, such cases force the country to confront a collective shame. They raise questions around human morality, diminishing trust and affection in society, and breakdowns in the legal justice system. In the face of these atrocities, women took to the streets, demanding justice and accountability. But their calls fell on deaf ears.
Pratistha Gautam’s story

“I was 11 years old when I was sexually abused by my close maternal uncle for four days,” said Pratishtha Gautam in an online interview with Global Voices in November 2026. Opening up about this incident was a real challenge for her, yet she was committed to sharing her story.

Her childhood was by no means easy. She moved regularly as a child, and at seven years old, she was sent to her maternal uncle’s house for a year because her parents had to move away to address her younger brother’s health issues.
It was in this house that a monster took away her innocence.

After four days of abuse, she escaped on the fifth day with the help of her neighbors. Finally getting a chance to flee from her abuser, she “rushed to my room, quickly happened to lock the door by chance, thankfully, and began to scream out to my neighbors.” She had witnessed men mistreating women in her neighborhood growing up and feels lucky that her cries weren’t met with indifference.

She felt neglected growing up and believed her parents loved her younger brother more. This left her with a sense of detachment from her family. The abuse only compounded her challenges. As she says, “It was not easy at all.”

The experience has left her with scars: “I have been awakened with nightmares since that incident, making my sleep extremely difficult.” She also suffers from panic attacks when she sees material about sexual abuse. She describes feeling like her heart is swollen and being torn apart. When triggered, she often freezes up and dissociates.

According to research from the American Academy of Pediatrics journal, child sexual abuse can be incredibly detrimental to a person’s long-term mental well-being. Child abuse survivors are more likely to suffer from anxiety disorders, depression, eating disorders and disturbances, sleep disruption and insomnia, and dissociation, as well as adverse physical health conditions and attachment issues, according to the Center of Expertise on Child Sexual Abuse.

This highlights the immense scale of pain that many children experience when they are victims of sexual abuse. Not everyone is able to speak out about such abuses. This is particularly true in South Asia, where there is a social stigma around abuse, due to entrenched ideas around “purity.”

She resents suggestions that it is women’s responsibility to not “tempt” men or draw attention to themselves. “Why should we be the ones to cover ourselves up?” she asks. She refuses to hide and stay silent while her abuser “is living free somewhere.” She refuses to remain invisible.

Even as many countries make strides in gender equality, gender-based violence continues to be a major issue. In a 2023 report, the World Health Organization (WHO) estimates that nearly one in three (31.6 percent) of women worldwide have been subjected to either physical and/or sexual violence in their lifetime — roughly 840 million women and girls.

At the root of gender-based violence lies a belief in male superiority. Not all men would openly endorse this belief, yet many see themselves as protectors of the women in their lives: their sisters, mothers, girlfriends, and wives. But this notion of protection is deeply flawed, especially when it comes at the cost of women’s freedom, mobility, access to opportunities, dreams, and agency.

Gautam recognizes this notion in her own upbringing. She had dreams of her own and was ready to chase them, but her family had a different plan for her. They wanted “to get me married off,” she said. She kept her independence through stubbornness and determination.
A trauma that persists

Today, Gautam lives in Adelaide in South Australia. She suffers from complex PTSD (post-traumatic stress disorder) and works as a mental health clinician helping other survivors of abuse. She reflected, in a heavy tone, on being a thousand miles away from home but safe and independent.
Image via Pratistha Gautam. Used with permission.

PTSD and insomnia aren’t the only consequences of her abuse. While she was once married, she struggled to cope with her trauma, and it negatively impacted her relationship, eventually leading to divorce.

As part of her treatment, Gautam has met regularly with psychotherapists over the years. Eventually, even that wasn’t enough. She put everything on hold for a year and gave herself time and space to focus on her mental health. She believes she would have difficulty living a normal life and still struggles with relationships. “I hate men. I used to hate them and still have trust issues,” she said.

Even as she struggles to process her own trauma, she also works to help others recover from abuse and offers pro bono psychological counseling. Being part of the solution has in some ways helped her heal. Her passion as a mental health clinician goes beyond her own individual experiences to the collective — a reminder to be empathetic as humans first.

While she primarily works in Australia, she is also committed to helping women back in her home country of Nepal. She has collaborated with Rakshya Nepal, an organization in Nepal that protects women and girls from sexual exploitation and trafficking.
Reflecting back on the choices she made, she said, “I cannot imagine if I could afford this luxury of mental space if I were not in Australia.”

This is also a testament to how South Asia treats survivors of sexual and physical abuse — even if they gather the courage to speak the truth, too often they are met with judgment and scorn. Part of this is due to limited regard for mental health, but it’s also about entrenched gender roles and strong societal expectations. There is a popular saying in Nepal reflecting these persistent gender dynamics: “timi ta chori manche ho ni” and “chora manche vayera gari halchan ni,” which roughly translates to “you are a girl, and boys will be boys.”
Written by Susmita Aryal

8288df491a7a07bc: TOKYO: Magnetic tape, once widely used in cassette and video tapes, is drawing renewed interest, with its ability to provide large offline storage capacity prompting a major supplier to sharply ramp up output amid the rise of artificial intelligence-driven cyberattacks, Kyodo News reported.
Fujifilm Holdings Corp. said recently that it plans to increase its magnetic tape production capacity fivefold from fiscal 2025 levels.

The company said it will invest about ¥10 billion (US$63 million) to expand capacity at its facility in Odawara, Kanagawa Prefecture, by fiscal 2028, manufacturing latest-generation products with capacities of up to 100 terabytes for use in AI data centres and elsewhere.

Demand for magnetic tape declined as flash memory and external hard drives became mainstream storage media. But the company continued technological development, including efforts to increase capacity.
Magnetic tape can store data offline, protecting it against ransomware and other cyberattacks by physically isolating it from networks.
Besides Fujifilm, the only other major magnetic tape manufacturer in Japan is Sony Storage Media Corp., based in Tagajo, Miyagi Prefecture.

5447b6121194e800: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hopes MCA will engage its grassroots members to explain why the coalition has chosen to work with Perikatan Nasional in three state elections.
He acknowledged that MCA members might have differing opinions on the cooperation with the PAS-led coalition, adding that this was normal.

“This (cooperation) was decided by the top (BN) leadership... I want MCA to help its grassroots members understand why BN has taken this approach,” he said when officiating MCA’s general assembly here.

“As Umno president, I want the Malay and Muslim communities to find common ground and work together on matters where we share common views,” he said, describing the approach as “tafahum siyasi”, or political understanding.
Zahid also reiterated that BN represented the voices of all Malaysians and repeated the coalition’s pledge to reintroduce the goods and services tax (GST) if it took over the federal government.
He added that regardless of which coalitions or parties BN worked with, its identity and principles would remain intact.
MCA secretary-general Chong Sin Woon yesterday said MCA is open to the possibility of cooperating with other parties, citing the country’s complex political landscape.
Chong’s remarks on cooperating with other parties come in the wake of BN’s alliance with PN in recent state elections.
BN won 48 seats after going solo in Johor, then formed an alliance with PN in Negeri Sembilan and Melaka – a cooperation which secured 25 and 24 seats in the respective states.
At the Johor polls in July, PAS called on its members and supporters to vote for Umno or BN candidates in state constituencies where PN was not contesting.
Don't fight over local council elections, says Zahid
Zahid also urged MCA Youth chief Ling Tian Soon and Umno Youth chief Dr Akmal Saleh to resolve their public disagreement over local council elections.
“Please don't fight. This is not a big issue,” he said jokingly in Mandarin.
Yesterday, MCA Youth passed a resolution calling on the government to revive local council elections, starting with the federal territories.
The federal territories of Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Labuan do not have state legislative assemblies.
Ling said local council elections would give residents the opportunity to elect their representatives, just as voters in other states elect their assemblymen.
Akmal subsequently criticised MCA Youth’s proposal, saying its position was not shared by Umno Youth or BN Youth.

Umno has repeatedly opposed reviving local council elections, citing costs to taxpayers, concerns over greater racial polarisation and the view that state assemblies already perform the necessary functions.
Local council elections were suspended in 1965, following the declaration of a state of emergency during the Indonesia-Malaysia confrontation, and effectively abolished in 1966.

4e9712c2cccc34aa: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional will leave it to Negeri Sembilan Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir to decide on the appointment of the state’s menteri besar, says coalition chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

77d1e3111ca54c5b: SEOUL: South Korea's education minister resigned Sunday over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted ahead of the country's key college entrance exams last week.

The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday, when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score, just four days before the crucial college entrance exam known as the Suneung.
The annual nine-hour Suneung is widely seen as a ticket to prestigious universities, well-paid jobs and even better marriage prospects in the highly competitive country.

The confession sent officials scrambling to roll out a slew of preventive measures – including blocking public Wi-Fi in testing areas and placing stickers over clothing buttons – but education minister Choi Kyo-jin struggled to reassure the public, particularly after remarks he made three days before the exam.

"The exam concluded without any major incidents... However, as the minister in charge, I do not believe I am immune from public criticism that we failed to prepare adequately in advance," Choi wrote on X.
"Now that the exam is over, I take full responsibility and hereby offer my resignation," he added.
President Lee Jae Myung has accepted his resignation, the presidential office said.

Asked during a parliamentary hearing on Monday whether he was confident that authorities could catch would-be cheaters on exam day, the 72-year-old replied, "Due to my age, I am not confident I could."
His response quickly drew public backlash.
Choi did not appear at press conferences in the days leading up to Thursday's exam, where a vice minister instead announced the preventive measures.

Officials said 111 cases of misconduct involving electronic devices were identified during Thursday's exam, nearly half of which were detected through three emergency alerts sent by the government to identify smartphones that test takers had failed to hand over.

6f2d9f153e249ab8: Following the 2026 state elections, many are predicting that Umno and Perikatan Nasional (PN) will team up and win power in the next general election (GE).

Most analysts see it as an almost certain clash between PH and a PAS-led PN in the peninsula. Some argue that GE16 will be fought primarily on traditional flashpoints: Malay rights, Islamic values, economic delivery, and non-Malay frustrations.
That may be true, but I think this election is more likely to boil down to a dramatic contest of political agility and manoeuvres between Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Anwar Ibrahim.

While East Malaysia’s blocs in Sabah and Sarawak will—as always—play a decisive kingmaker role post-election to protect local autonomy, the battle to capture Putrajaya itself remains a peninsula-driven contest. Within that crucible, GE16 will essentially be a battle of wills and operational skill between two men who know how to survive at the top.

Zahid's core competency is political engineering. He treats relationships as leverage, public statements as bargaining signals, and possesses a feel for power dynamics that is probably unmatched in modern Malaysian politics.

Yet, while his "blue wave" narrative resonates powerfully with Malay voters, it does not travel cleanly to the urban, mixed, and non-Malay constituencies that ultimately decide a national majority—though Umno relies on its traditional Barisan Nasional coalition mechanisms to manage multi-ethnic seats.

Conversely, Anwar’s strength lies in policy, narrative, and survival. A reformist with international credibility and a coherent platform, Anwar has ridden the waves of triumph and defeat, navigated various crises, and risen to become prime minister.
He is waging a war of attrition, using his control over the national budget and administrative levers to delay the electoral clock while Zahid tries to force an early hand.
To understand why this duel will define GE16, we must look back at how their paths have intertwined over the last three decades.

When the bitter fallout between then-Umno president Mahathir Mohamad and his deputy Anwar erupted in the late 1990s, Zahid—serving as Umno Youth chief—initially backed Anwar. Yet, after Anwar’s sacking in 1998, Zahid quickly pivoted, reconciled with Mahathir, and demonstrated the classic Umno survival instinct: prioritising pragmatism over loyalty.

From that point, Zahid embarked on a meticulously calculated ascent: consolidating his base in Perak, building a formidable personal network, becoming Umno’s deputy president, and finally taking the top spot in 2018.

Following the 2022 humiliation when Umno won just 26 seats, calls for his resignation mounted. He weathered the storm, teamed up with Anwar to secure the post of deputy prime minister, and used his proximity to power to reassert Umno’s relevance.

Anwar, for his part, pursued his long game: forming PKR, driving the Reformasi movement, riding the 2008 opposition surge, and eventually making an uneasy truce with his arch-rival Mahathir to wrest power in 2018. But political betrayals caused Mahathir’s government to collapse, paving the way for short-lived administrations under Muhyiddin Yassin and Ismail Sabri Yaakob.

The inconclusive 2022 general election threw Anwar and Zahid together into an improbable partnership. Zahid secured ministerial perks and shared authority, and by December 2025, the Attorney General’s Chambers granted him a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) on the 47 corruption charges involving the Yayasan Akalbudi fund.
Critics blasted the move as a classic manoeuvre to shield allies and buy loyalty, though it has consistently been denied.
Since then, Zahid has supercharged Umno's stature among Malay supporters by leaning into the reliable narrative of Malay unity and perceived threats to Malay dominance.

The resulting PAS-Umno tactical cooperation benefits both parties. This momentum was reflected in the 2026 state elections, though formulas varied: in Johor, BN swept 48 of 56 seats alone (while PN supporters were quietly instructed to back BN in uncontested seats), whereas in Negeri Sembilan and Melaka, BN and PN formally shared seats.
True to form, Zahid is keeping all options open by refusing to commit to a formal GE16 pact with PN, executing a masterstroke that forces both PH and PN to compete for Umno's favour.

Simultaneously, he has tightened his internal grip: the Umno Supreme Council has postponed party polls to a date no later than six months after GE16, and an "unconditional open-door" policy has welcomed back former rivals like Khairy Jamaluddin and Hishammuddin Hussein. Zahid is building a broad electoral coalition while keeping his own leadership uncontested.

Demonstrating his pragmatic ambition further, Zahid acknowledged Gabungan Parti Sarawak's (GPS) absolute regional dominance by confirming that BN would sit out the Sarawak state election to respect East Malaysian autonomy and keep the federal focus razor-sharp on the peninsula.

Conversely, Anwar’s Pakatan Harapan has been battling severe internal friction. PKR has suffered heavy blows: high-profile figures like Rafizi Ramli and Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad departed to form Parti Bersama Malaysia, Nurul Izzah went on indefinite leave as deputy president, and the party suffered a major rout in Melaka.

Anwar's prospects now hinge heavily on timing. PH’s parliamentary term runs until December 2027, with GE16 legally due by February 2028. Every month of delay buys both sides different advantages: Zahid consolidates his machine, while Anwar attempts to deliver tangible economic relief.
If Anwar can produce visible improvements in the cost of living by late 2027 and push through more reforms, the votes will return.

Furthermore, PH retains a structural edge in the urban and mixed constituencies that decide a national majority. State elections are typically less diverse and more heavily Malay-majority, making the "blue wave" less effective on a national scale.

Moreover, non-Malay support for PH is driven less by uncritical loyalty and more by a structural fear of the alternative (a PAS-led PN). As the Malay vote consolidates behind BN-PN, non-Malay voters increasingly rally behind DAP and PH as a defensive counterweight, keeping PH viable nationally even as it bleeds support in heartland seats.
Also, as seat negotiations between Umno and PAS heat up, deep fractures in the Malay-Muslim vote will be exposed.

Yet, as these electoral calculations play out, Zahid carries a heavy legal overhang. The Court of Appeal allowed the Malaysian Bar's judicial review challenge in May 2026, the Federal Court granted Zahid and the AG leave to appeal in October 2026, and the High Court has slated case management for June 2027, with the full hearing deferred until the Federal Court appeal concludes. It is a sword of Damocles that is certain to become a major campaign issue.

Ultimately, GE16 will be a contest of political operators. The 2026 state elections suggest Zahid holds the momentum. However, Anwar’s control over the electoral timeline, his economic levers, and the structural divide between state and national electorates keep the race wide open.

What began as a clash between reform and patronage has evolved into a masterclass in machine politics versus institutional statecraft. The next general election will not be decided by slogans or promises alone—it will be decided by who plays the sharper game over the next six to twelve months.

52e6204978a8560b: The Najib Razak saga has, in many ways, eclipsed even Anwar Ibrahim’s ‘Reformasi’ struggles, which saw many of us old-timers go through some very harrowing times.
Both were deputy prime ministers and served under Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
Their parallels are striking. Anwar was sacked, charged, convicted and spent time in prison before being pardoned, later rising to become prime minister.
Najib took the opposite route. An Umno prime minister, no less, he lost power, was charged, convicted and served time, before being pardoned twice, albeit conditionally.

Despite the unbridled demonisation of the DAP and non-Malays as traitors out to wreck a nation, it must be stressed that it was a courageous Malay judge—a woman no less—who sent the former Umno president to jail.
Now, there are many “firsts” in this saga.

Najib went on trial in what became known as “the world’s largest kleptocracy case”, a notorious distinction that brought his party and the country the sort of international headlines it could have done without.
Secondly, Najib is the first prime minister to be incarcerated in Malaysia.
And thirdly, this is the first documented house arrest case in the country, even preceding a proposed new law that the government intends to introduce in Parliament.
Now there are many views about the former Pekan MP’s house arrest.
Among them is the perceived double-standard. Why is Najib allowed these perks, while other convicts are not?
There is also the matter of the king’s decision in Najib’s pardon application. Must the king adhere to the pardon board’s advice? And should the minutes have been declassified?
As for the king’s decision to allow Najib to be placed under house arrest, that is his prerogative, one that is enshrined in our Federal Constitution.
He has chosen to exercise it in Najib’s favour for reasons known only to him. Not being privy to that decision, and without any insights into his reasons, it would not be proper to comment on it.
But it has to be emphasised that there is no prefect constitution, no perfect rendition of history, and no perfect interpretation of religion.
Hence, we need to rely on the wisdom and experience of those who make such decisions with the nation’s best interests at heart.
The recent publication of the minutes of that meeting of the pardons board has given the public a rare insight into what transpired and the stance taken by each board member.
That said, the published document should not trigger a blame game.
Whatever one feels about the decision, it must be acknowledged that it went through due process.
If Malaysians believe that process should be improved or changed, the proper avenue is through their elected representatives in the Dewan Rakyat.
For my part, I am satisfied that due process has been observed and therefore respect and accept the decision reached.

Still, I find it comical that Umno has been so worked up over the declassification of the document simply because it was not accompanied by a royal decree, even arguing that the omission was somehow tantamount to disrespecting the Malay rulers.
Has that same respect been shown to Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir amid the seemingly unending constitutional crisis in Negeri Sembilan, a controversy that bears Umno's fingerprints all over it?
The time has come for us to put the brouhaha over Najib's house arrest to rest.
At the end of the day, Najib was convicted for a crime, served some time in jail, applied for a pardon, as allowed by law, and was granted one.
Placing him under house arrest does not erase his criminal conviction.
There is no value in bickering over the merits of the house arrest as it serves no purpose other than to instigate one party and weaponise the issue.
It is time we focused on the more important stuff, like the bread-and-butter issues affecting ordinary Malaysians. That is a far more worthy cause.

9b6b75dea9243402: Tony Pua has apparently discovered a remarkable constitutional innovation: when the king grants clemency against objections, publish the objections and call it accountability. Yet the awkward question remains. Does displaying dissent explain the constitutional decision, or merely provide political cover for those embarrassed by its outcome?
On Nov 18, Pua circulated pages described as declassified minutes from the Sept 18 Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning former prime minister Najib Razak.

According to news reports, Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar and federal territories minister Hannah Yeoh opposed house arrest. The king nevertheless approved a conditional pardon. These reported extracts warrant authentication and contextual examination; a Facebook upload is not itself a constitutional certificate.
Let us distinguish three matters politicians seem determined to blend: the right to disagree during deliberations, the authority to decide, and the legality of disclosing deliberations afterwards.

Article 42 establishes the constitutional pardoning framework. Recording objections does not confer a veto. Nor does royal authority automatically exempt officials from explaining how records were classified, accessed and released.

Pua’s intervention invites sharper scrutiny precisely because he presents disclosure as vindication. Vindication of what? That DAP representatives objected? The minutes reportedly establish that much. That the government’s political conscience is therefore spotless? That is a considerably longer leap, requiring evidence rather than screenshots and self-congratulation.

DAP cannot simultaneously celebrate constitutional procedure when it documents ministerial dissent and treat the resulting royal decision as someone else’s political inconvenience. A constitutional monarchy is not a buffet where parties select the minutes they enjoy and leave the decision behind. If dissent was properly recorded, publicly explain it. If the decision was lawful, respect it. Neither proposition requires surrendering criticism of corruption.

Umno is justified in demanding a clear account of the disclosure process. Its leaders have asked whether the documents were officially declassified, who authorised circulation, and whether the palace was consulted. Those are legitimate institutional questions, although assertions that publication necessarily constitutes an insult to the king require a specific legal and factual foundation. Defending royal dignity should strengthen constitutional precision, not replace it with outrage.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim faces the more uncomfortable examination. He has publicly defended every prisoner’s access to the pardon process and acknowledged the king’s constitutional role. Fine words. But was his administration’s handling of disclosure governed by a consistent rule, or by whichever political controversy happened to be burning that week? The public deserves an answer from Putrajaya, not another seminar on principles everyone claims to cherish.

The comparison with Anwar’s 2018 pardon is unavoidable. Wan Saiful Wan Jan has called for those Pardons Board minutes to be released, too. That demand does not prove irregularity in either pardon. It does expose the weakness of selective transparency. If publication serves public confidence today, what principled distinction governs disclosure of earlier proceedings? Privacy, privilege and national security may justify redactions; political convenience is not a constitutional doctrine.

There is an important qualification. Minutes capture deliberation, not necessarily every legal consideration or the full operative instrument. Readers should resist pretending five circulated pages settle all constitutional questions. Officials must establish authenticity, classification status, completeness, and applicable disclosure authority before political protagonists announce their preferred verdict.

My assessment is that this affair tests the government’s credibility more severely than Najib’s political fortunes. A government preaching institutional reform must demonstrate procedures that survive partisan advantage. Publish a reasoned disclosure policy, identify the competent authorising authority, and apply equivalent standards to comparable pardons. Where confidentiality is required, explain its legal basis without exposing protected deliberations.

And Pua? He is entitled to criticise Najib, challenge clemency and defend his former colleagues. He is not entitled to confuse proof of opposition with proof of governmental consistency. The former may fit neatly into a social media post; the latter demands accountability across administrations, personalities, and inconvenient precedents.
The king does not require politicians to manufacture unanimity. The Constitution requires institutions to understand their responsibilities.
Umno should defend that distinction firmly; DAP and PH should answer it without theatrical evasion; Anwar should insist upon rules rather than improvisation.
When constitutional records become partisan ammunition, the real scandal is not disagreement. It is a government unable to explain who loaded the weapon, under what authority, and why only now.
Azam Mohd is an FMT reader.
